text:
Alex: heads up — after the 02:15 kernel swap (fused-attn v2 -> v2b) we saw a sharp drop in prefix/prompt cache hit rate for rdx-3b-quant in prod. baseline ~81% -> ~44% for requests with short priming prompts. rolling averages moved in ~10m.
Maya: omg, that's big. do we have a sample query set that reproduces it?
Alex: yes. running the usual perf harness (./tools/prefix_eval.sh --model rdx-3b-quant --profile small_prompts) gives consistent repro locally. attaching quick logs: 
```
[2026-03-18T02:23:11Z] prefix_cache: lookup key=sha1(priming+norm) -> MISS
[2026-03-18T02:23:11Z] kv_store: stored_key=...a3f, retrieved_key=...b3f (len equal)
[2026-03-18T02:23:11Z] kernel: fused_attn_v2b variant selected for seq=64
```
Chris: interesting that stored vs retrieved key differ by a few bytes. could be normalization / tokenizer change or kernel reorder affecting prefix fingerprint. did the kernel swap touch tokenization path?
Alex: kernel change strictly in attention path, but the compile changed layout for fused matmul which altered padding behavior and we also flipped a tiny quant rounding tweak in the model loader during the rollout. suspect either padding normalization or a subtle float->int hash change.
Sam: runtime-bot shows the deploy: 
```
runtime-bot: deploy completed rdx-3b-quant @ 2026-03-18T02:15:06Z (k8s rs: fused-attn-v2b)
```
Maya: can you run a binary compare on cache keys pre/post? maybe a small script to regen keys for same prompts under both runtimes.
Alex: done that — created key dumps from stable node (pre-swap) and current node. differences are localized to prefix whitespace-normalization and last-token padding bytes. sample: 
```
pre: "priming=\"Summarize:\"\n\n"
post: "priming=\"Summarize:\"\n\u0000"
```
so a null padding byte sneaks in after compilation change.
Chris: aha. padding introduced by new matmul tiling that uses 8-byte alignment, we saw similar in a perf branch long ago. hashing code uses raw bytes; nulls change hashes.
Maya: is this only for quant models or affects fp16 too?
Alex: reproduces across quant and fp16 but threshold of hit-loss is worse for quant because our key builder includes quantized kernel outputs for a small cached fingerprint step. quant path happens to materialize padding earlier.
Sam: mitigation ideas: 1) canonicalize keys by trimming trailing \u0000 in key builder; 2) normalize tokenizer output; 3) revert kernel tiling.
Chris: trimming trailing nulls + adding a unit test would be fastest. low-risk. but need to ensure we don't accidentally strip meaningful zeros (rare). maybe only strip repeated terminal zeros when tokenization produced no explicit \u0000.
Alex: I prototyped a patch: in engine/kv_key.cpp before sha1: apply remove_trailing_padding(bytes, allowed_pad=8). small microbenchmark shows no perf regression (~0.3% wall).
Maya: run a canary on dedicated pool? we should validate hit-rate and ensure no correctness regressions for embeddings.
Alex: launching canary with patch on 3 nodes now. harness run: ./tools/prefix_eval.sh --canary --patch trim-pad --samples 2000. will report soon.
Chris: also add a tracing tag when we store prefix keys that contains kernel_variant and padding_len — helps debug future tiling rollouts.
Alex: added trace: store_event { key_hash, kernel_variant: "fused-attn-v2b", pad_len: 1 }
runtime-bot: canary: 3 nodes patched; traffic split 5%.
Maya: great. what's timeline for rollback if canary doesn't heal?
Sam: plan: 1) if hit-rate < 70% after 30m -> automated rollback to fused-attn-v2; 2) notify infra oncall; 3) revert quant loader tweak in a follow-up.
Alex: canary results after 15m: hit-rate improved from 44% -> 79% on patched nodes. logs show pad_len mostly 0 now.
Maya: nice! push the patch to release branch + small unit test covering trailing-zero normalization.
Chris: follow-up: add CI gate that runs key-stability test when changing kernels or compile flags — spin up tiny model and assert identical key fingerprints for canonical prompts across variants.
Alex: filing a short doc in eng-runtime/ops: prefix-keying-guidelines + linking to the test. cc @Maya @Chris.
Maya: thanks. can we close the thread after merge + rollback aborted?
Sam: will monitor for 1h then close. :thumbsup:
